answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a handwritten daily ledger kept with a quill, each entry a cipher from that morning's unpredictable public weather reading at a named station. Independent verifiers mirror the ledger: on random spot-checks the holder must reproduce the day's cipher live on camera, holding the page to a mirror so the ink proves it is the same sheet. One hand cannot keep two daily journals, and the verifier fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another ledger, another daily hand, and twice the prior fee.
